actions.action: Tap branches over white paper to confirm thrips
Place blue or yellow sticky traps near plants
Test alcohol spray on a single leaf before wider use
Inspect all 80+ plants, especially orchids and blooming plants
Inspect new plant purchases before adding them to the collection
Cut off badly damaged leaves and infested flowers and bag them
Spray insecticidal soap, neem or spinosad every 3-5 days for 3-6 weeks, rotating products
Apply a soil drench or top-dressing to kill pupae
Repot heavily infested plants in fresh media
Release predatory mites (A. swirskii/cucumeris) or Orius
For severe cases, use a systemic insecticide like imidacloprid
Keep monitoring sticky traps for several weeks after thrips disappear

reason: The answer correctly identifies thrips, but the beneficial-insect program that worked is only one of many suggestions and framed as 'possibly', and nothing recommended is likely to harm the plant.
